messages:
maya: Heads-up — I'm seeing a steady memory growth in KV residency for a handful of longctx tenants, leading to paging spikes on p-agg nodes this morning. pprof attached to the thread.
aj: Can you drop the pprof link and a quick top-line? how big is the growth and which tenants?
maya: Quick summary: +20% resident pages over 6 hours for tenant t-42 and t-88, paging spikes ≈ 150ms tail on some requests. Not steady leak but very high reuse churn + fragmentation.
maya: snippet from node logs: 
```
[2026-03-18T09:12:03Z] KV_RESIDENCY_UPDATE tenant=t-42 delta=+1.2M pages resident=6.8M reused=2.1M evicted=3.9M
[2026-03-18T09:12:04Z] PAGING_EVENT node=p-agg-12 dur=162ms pages=278
```
aj: hmm. did anything change in batching or kernel selection for those models? longer seq lengths will blow up KV usage.
maya: Noted — there was a rollout last night of the batching heuristic that increases max batch window for GPU kernels when avg seq > 1k. Could be related.
devin: If long batches keep KV alive longer (larger KV cache per request) that can accentuate fragmentation and reduce reuse. Do we have per-tenant residency watermarks?
lia: We have soft quotas but they are permissive. The soft quota only emits metrics and kicks eviction after pretty high deltas.
ricardo: If the kernel selection change prefers fused kernels that keep larger activation buffers mapped, we might get longer-lived pages pinned. Need to correlate kernel selection logs with KV residency.
maya: I ran a quick correlation: for t-42, 78% of requests chose the new fused kernel after the rollout; residency increase aligns.
ops-bot: alert: KV_PAGING_HIGH host=p-agg-12 severity=warning metric=kv.paging.rate value=0.34
aj: Proposed short-term mitigation: 1) revert batching window tweak for the affected model graph, or 2) tighten per-tenant soft quota to start evict earlier for noisy tenants. Which is faster?
devin: Option 2 is quick to flip in config, but it might cause higher miss rate for latency-sensitive tenants. Option 1 needs a rollback and verification.
lia: We can also try a tuned eviction policy: prefer zero-hit pages first (low reuse score) and prioritize compaction of fragmented slabs. That reduces tail without full eviction.
ricardo: Agree. Also consider sampling-based residency accounting: only keep precise residency for top-K hot prefixes, approximate the rest. Cuts maintenance overhead.
maya: I pushed a temporary rule: t-42,t-88 => soft_quota_multiplier=0.6. Observability: residency growth slowed within 10 minutes but paging tail still present.
aj: Nice. Can you paste the quick pprof flame for the hotspot? suspicious functions: kv::page_walk, kernel_fused::alloc_state
maya: pasted below (cropped):
```
- kv::page_walk 32%
- kv::evict_scan 18%
- kernel_fused::alloc_state 12%
- batching::window_manager 8%
- io::page_flush 4%
```
lia: kv::evict_scan high suggests we're scanning large slabs before eviction decision -> expensive. We should maintain per-slab approximate reuse histograms so scans are O(1) for hotness.
devin: Also, for longctx flows we should cap per-request KV reservation. Right now we allocate based on seq len * stride which is unbounded for some models. Add a per-request cap (e.g., 64MB) and trade off a small additional refill for bounding residency.
ricardo: For fairness we need quota enforcement tied to token accounting at the API layer. If a tenant's token rate is low but they keep huge residency, that's a fairness hole. Enforcement steps: 1) meter tokens -> 2) derive residency allowance -> 3) enforce eviction priority.
aj: We're worried about perf regressions if eviction thrashes. Any quick experiment to test compaction-first policy?
maya: I ran a staging experiment: compaction-first reduced tail by ~30% no added misses. Config: `evict_policy=compaction_first; compaction_threshold=0.2`
lia: Can we add a lightweight background compactor that triggers when fragmentation ratio > 0.15 and node idle < 20%? cheap win.
ops-bot: deploy-bot: canary deploy queued by maya for eng-runtime@compactor-v2 to 2 nodes.
devin: Longer term: integrate kernel selection signal into the scheduler so we can predict KV residency cost per request and preemptively throttle or route to nodes with spare residency. Kernel selection must emit cost_estimate with model/runtime.
maya: Good idea. Also want a tenancy score: recent_residency_rate + token_rate -> isolation_score. Use it to proportionally limit residency when node-wide pressure.
ricardo: Also need alerting tweaks: surface per-tenant residency percentiles and per-tenant fragmentation ratio. Current alerts are node-global only.
aj: Action items: 
- maya: roll back batching tweak for affected model or keep soft quota flip (short-term) — update by EOD.
- lia/devin: prototype compaction-first background job + per-slab reuse histogram (next 3 days).
- ricardo: design token->residency quota mapping and runbook (2 days).
- aj: add kernel selection cost_estimate scaffold to trace logs (this week).
maya: marking follow-ups in a GH issue and link here: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/issues/789
lia: I'll add pager notes and update alerts.
ricardo: +1. thanks all. :thumbsup:
maya: thanks — will keep thread updated with metrics after the config flips.
